A drying drop pins its contact line, so the footprint cannot shrink.
Evaporation removes liquid fastest at the thin edge, and the only
replacement source is the interior — an outward flow develops and carries
suspended particles to the rim[^1].

See also [the long page](long-page.qmd) and [the home page](../index.qmd).

[^1]: Deegan et al., *Nature* 389, 827 (1997).
